heroHeadline: PLA Pauses Air Sorties on May 6 (0 Aircraft, 7 PLAN Vessels) — First Zero-Sortie Day Since Pre-Record Surge; Defense Budget 4th Round Fails; Floor Vote Possible May 8; 8 Days to Trump-Xi Beijing Summit
heroSubtitle: PLA's May 2 surge to 29 sorties (new non-exercise record, surpassing the April 26 peak of 28) has been followed by a steady cooling: 1 sortie (May 3) → 2 sorties (May 4) → 1 sortie (May 5) → 0 sorties (May 6), the first zero-sortie day since before the record surge. PLA naval presence of 7 PLAN vessels + 1 official ship continues as the maritime component of its cross-strait deterrence posture even with air activity suspended. Taiwan's defense budget fourth cross-party negotiation round concluded May 6 without consensus — the KMT's NT$380B plan and TPP's NT$400B cap remain opposed to the DPP's full NT$1.25 trillion request. The bill has completed its mandatory cooling period; a floor vote is legally possible from May 8. Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim said the budget 'shows Taiwan's will to defend itself.' With 8 days remaining before the Trump-Xi Beijing summit (May 14-15), Taiwan's failure to pass the budget weakens its negotiating position as Xi is expected to press Trump on limiting future US arms sales. TSMC's $56B AI expansion and strong Q1 2026 earnings (+58% YoY profit) signal the semiconductor sector remains resilient despite mounting cross-strait pressure.
